Question: Crowding out

Options: 
A. occurs when interest rates fall due to government borrowing.
B. occurs when consumers and firms spend less offsetting expansionary fiscal policy.
C. occurs when the government reduces its spending in response to inflation.
D. is a consequence of contractionary fiscal policy.
E. is one reason fiscal policy is so effective.
F. is when expansionary fiscal policy leads to a decrease in interest rates.
G. happens when the government increases taxes to reduce the budget deficit.
H. causes the aggregate demand curve to shift to the right.

Provide the correct letter choice in \boxed{X}, where X is the correct letter choice. Keep the explanation or feedback within 3 sentences.

    *   Definition: In macroeconomics, the crowding-out effect occurs when government expenditure and/or discounted increases in revenues (like tax cuts/tax reductions) lead to a reduction in consumption and investment. This is typically caused by the government borrowing more money, which increases the supply of loanable funds, driving up interest rates. Higher interest rates then discourage private investment spending (and sometimes consumption).
